I had a very upsetting experience with this groomer, and I feel responsible to warn other pet owners. This was my puppy’s first professional grooming, and instead of guiding me properly, they advised a full cut even though my puppy was only four months old and still had puppy hair. His whiskers and eyebrows were cut excessively, and the grooming was poorly done overall. They also used an overpowering perfume that caused irritation, and his paws were not trimmed correctly.

Within hours, my puppy began scratching nonstop. For four days he got worse, and he eventually had to be taken to the ER on Halloween night. We spent six hours there and I ended up paying over $2,000 for treatment, medications, and de-parasitizing. The vet confirmed that he had parasites and severe irritation. The medication led to diarrhea, dehydration, and lethargy for nearly a week. The total cost of everything that followed was close to $3,000.

When I reached out to the groomer to explain what happened and request a refund, he refused. He also did not return my calls afterward. Instead of addressing the issue, he only offered to groom my puppy again, which obviously was not an option after what happened.

They also requested me to give him medication which ended up giving him the diarrea, so it is his responsibility.

A first grooming should be a peaceful and positive experience. Instead, this turned into one of the worst and most stressful situations I’ve been through with my puppy. It has been a month and he is still recovering.

I strongly recommend choosing another groomer. If anything goes wrong here, they will not take responsibility, and you will be left to deal with the consequences on your own.

I also have no need for someone to "pay for my service", the medical records say that my puppy was brought by constant scratching and stomach issues BOTH CAUSED BY GROOMER AND UNDER GROOMER CARE.

The poor little dog looked awful. I showed a picture of what I wanted; if they don't know how to do it, it would have been better to say so. Sometimes you need to use scissors, not just clippers. The end result was a dog with almost no hair and an uneven cut. A complete disaster.
